description:
jobs/source.rs scope_code walks a source owner's surface in order, and every function it scopes is stashed as FactKey::FunctionSourceStash(f), claimed by the job ScopeCode(owner). When the walk meets an item macro it returns ScopePublication::Blocked(effects) with the stashes so far as outputs and a wait on the macro's expansion, which is a nested root's backend product. Two consequences, both measured with instrumented scheduler.rs quiescent_cone and jobs/mod.rs on the reproducer below; each alone leaves all 11 stalled tests red, fixing both turns all 82 tests in the selection green.

Layer 1, dirtiness: while ScopeCode(owner) waits, every stash it has claimed is dirty. The macro's own source is one of them (FunctionId(36) below IS the macro): the walk stashes it, then waits on FunctionDefined(36), which is reached only through PublishFunctionSource(36) -> FunctionSourceStash(36), the walk's own dirty claim. Under the strict drain rule (fz-kdt.227) that is refused: "refuse asked=Recursive(36) dirty=FunctionSourceStash(36) publishers=[ScopeCode(17)]".

Layer 2, read set: after the expansion arrives and ScopeCode(owner) concludes, it is a clean publisher of FunctionSourceStash(36), but its read set is the whole walk's, including product_reads on the macro's expansion product. So the stash of a function defined ABOVE the macro is grounded in the macro's own product, and the cone beneath the product's own compile reaches the product being driven: RootEntry(3) <- SeedRoot(3) <- Recursive(36) <- StaticCallees(36) <- LoweredBody(36) <- FunctionDefined(36) <- ExpandedFunctionSource(36) <- FunctionSource(36) <- FunctionSourceStash(36) <- ScopeCode(17) reads Product{root 3}. Across the 11 tests every layer-2 refusal is on the product of the very root under arbitration (90 refusals, no exception). Dropping ScopeCode's product_reads on conclusion, together with the layer-1 fix, is sufficient: the false dependency is the whole of layer 2.

Reproducer:
  defmacro define_answer() do
    {:def, %{}, [{:answer, %{}, []}, [{:do, 9}]]}
  end
  define_answer()
  def main(), do: answer()
Stalled tests under the strict rule (11 by name; the earlier count of 12 included a census pin): compiler2_test def_and_defp_bounce_through_definition_macros_and_preserve_visibility, jobs/body_test quote_preserves_keyword_tuples_in_a_generated_function_definition, macro_product_test source_less_item_macro_output_round_trips_without_fabricated_provenance, port_macros_test item_macro_compiler_ast_splices_callable_fn + item_macro_list_of_compiler_ast_functions_splices_multiple_fns, port_misc_test multiple_test_blocks_compile + test_macro_failing_assert_compiles + test_macro_passing_assert_compiles, product_drive_test standalone_drive_owns_the_prefix_before_a_nested_root_product_session, source_publish_test source_publication_accepts_raw_compiler_fragments_from_item_macros + source_publication_expands_item_macros_as_scope_fragments.

Research: the scheduler has no derivation identity. FactSlot.publishers, dirty_publishers, unfinal_publishers and read_finality are keyed by bare Job (facts.rs ~183, scheduler.rs). fz-tfn.41's "(Job, DerivationId)" describes the Job enum's own payload, not a second field. World::demand_fact_producer has deliberately no arm for FunctionSourceStash (drive.rs ~517-545): it rides ScopeCode's conclusion, and publish_function_source_job (jobs/source.rs ~340-376) depends on that being the only arm-less wait. A blanket scheduler rule "a blocked job's this-run outputs are concluded" is unsound: on 00181, DeriveRuntimeDemand (15), AnalyzeActivation (15, incl. cumulative ReturnType and ActivationInputs), SeedRoot (4) and DefineModule (1, 80 stashes) all publish while blocked.

Design (pending the user's decision): exact ownership by scope segment. A scope walk is a sequence of segments separated by item macros. Segment k is its own job, reading the previous segment's namespace and the k-1th expansion product, scoping until the next macro, concluding with the namespace so far and the stashes of the functions it scoped. A stash's publisher is then a job that concludes (layer 1) whose reads are exactly that function's ground: the namespace above it and the products of the macros above it, never the product of a macro below it (layer 2). The blocked-with-claims shape in ScopePublication::Blocked goes away for ScopeCode. The final CodeScoped(owner) is concluded by the walk that reads the last segment. The arm-less FunctionSourceStash demand keeps riding CodeScoped's demand. Rejected alternative: teach the drain to treat the product under arbitration as a cycle member; it hides the false dependency instead of removing it and would certify a real self-cycle through a macro's product instead of diagnosing it.
title: FunctionSourceStash(f) is claimed by the whole scope walk, so it inherits the walk's dirtiness and the walk's read set; neither belongs to f
